title: Following one render
summary: What happens between typing `vizx render explainer.json` and getting a page? Scroll through the steps; the diagram follows along.

steps.title: The CLI hands off
steps.text: [[cli]] does nothing clever: it calls [[build]] and decides what to do with the result. Without `--force`, any issue means nothing is written.

steps.title: Parse and check the document
steps.text: [[build]] reads the JSON and validates it against the [[schema]]. Then [[model]] checks cross-references: every `parent`, `from` and `to` must name a real entity.

steps.title: Gather the components
steps.text: [[registry]] starts from the built-ins and imports each custom module listed in the document. A module that doesn't look like a component is reported, not trusted.

steps.title: Walk the blocks
steps.text: [[engine]] visits each block, finds its component and validates the block's props against that component's schema. Errors carry the exact block path.

steps.title: Render code and diagrams
steps.text: Components ask the context for help. Code goes to [[code]], which highlights it with [[shiki]]; graphs are laid out by [[elk]]. Both happen at build time, so the page stays light.

steps.title: Assemble one file
steps.text: [[page]] wraps everything in the shell and inlines [[theme]], [[runtime]] and the CSS and scripts of only the components that were used.

children.text: The same story, in time order:

messages.label: buildExplainer(path)
messages.note: The CLI only parses arguments and delegates.

messages.label: parse + validate JSON
messages.note: JSON syntax, the document schema, then cross-references.

messages.label: loadRegistry(components)
messages.note: Built-ins plus the document's custom modules.

messages.label: renderBlocks(blocks)
messages.note: Blocks render in parallel; each gets a context scoped to its path.

messages.label: validate props
messages.note: Each block's props are checked against its component's schema.

messages.label: code(source)
messages.note: File reads and highlighting are cached per build.

messages.label: renderPage(parts)
messages.note: Only the CSS and scripts of components actually used are inlined.

messages.label: { html, issues }
messages.note: Issues are always returned; the CLI decides whether to write.

children.caption: The same journey as a sequence diagram. Hover a message or a note to pair them.

steps.title: Every block needs a type
steps.text: A block is any object with a `type`. Everything else is props.

steps.title: Find the component
steps.text: Unknown types are reported with a suggestion, e.g. `unknown component "grpah" (did you mean "graph"?)`.

steps.title: Validate props
steps.text: The component's own schema checks the props. Because built-ins use strict schemas, typos in prop names are caught too.

steps.title: Register in the outline
steps.text: Components can declare an outline title. That is how sections end up in the table of contents, and custom components can do the same.

steps.title: Render, safely
steps.text: The component renders with a context scoped to its path. If a custom component throws, the failure becomes an issue instead of a crash.
